notes: Web 436 — COUNT-PLUSONE-TEACHES-PEG (Nov 12, 2026; layers on web 435). The owner's order, Nov 12 ~13:28 CST, on the Aecon Trans day (card reading 4 counted by GPS, neither end pegged): the load he was just on did NOT count — counting has to be dynamic: when he taps +1 manually it should change the peg slightly, because that morning the job site moved his dump spot a few metres, the machine missed the count, and he +1'd it by hand. THE GAP, proven in the shipped code: counted events taught the site (the visit counter adopts proven faces as points; the peg counter drifts its centres on counted events; fence-recovery walks a centre toward a witnessed missed face) — but a manual +1 moved only the day's signed correction. The one signal that is ground truth by definition ("I tipped HERE") taught the site nothing, so the next tip at the moved face missed the same way. THE FIX (js/geoloads.js; one guarded call in js/app.js): (1) teachTip() on the dump-visit counter — a +1 at the tip (the counter's own last fix, held to the peg-planting 50 m accuracy bar; a rough or missing fix teaches nothing and the tap still counts) teaches the point set under the machine's own disciplines: within 100 m of a point it NUDGES that point toward where he actually tipped by at most the peg law's 25 m bounded step (his "change it slightly"); further out on the site's own ground the tap spot becomes a point of the site — a driver-proven face — out to the site's chain reach (the learned profile scale; the band beyond the 450 m shadow reach asks for the same loop-moved evidence the machine's own face adoption asks for); never within 450 m of a known other end (load-end ground is never taught as dump ground); never across town. (2) teachTip() on the peg counter — the same bounded lesson as a counted event's drift (25 m, honesty gate, site clamp, recovery-reach gate), without logging an event or moving any count; the drifted centre rides the snapshot. (3) nudge(+1) runs the lesson and, when it lands on the site's ground with the visit still open, marks the visit hand-counted against the TAUGHT ground — the v324 mark extended — and the visit counter's ingest now reports closedVisit (the other-end dwell confirmed), on which feedFix clears the mark: the v323 S6c discipline on this machine, so a tap whose visit closed uncounted STANDS and only the machine confirming the SAME tip retires it (no double count, no eaten next load). (4) A +1 in teach mode (no counter yet — the dump given out loud, never pinned) seeds the day's dump at the truck's position via GeoLoads.teachTap() — the navigated adoption's standard (known load site, peg-grade fix, a spot that pairs) — beginning present with the visit counted-in-state so that tip can never count twice, its count riding the correction like any armed-day tap. COUNTING LAW UNTOUCHED: a load is a dump-site visit; re-pegs bank the day count as always; the tap's load stays on the TAP side of the GPS/tap split forever — the lesson only teaches geometry, so the NEXT load at the moved spot is the one GPS counts by itself. Taught points ride the day snapshot (relaunch-safe). BENCH: new suite tools/count-plusone-teaches-peg-v436-test.js, 52/52, replaying the day at the glue level on the Nov 12 Aecon geometry — his morning (missed tip at a moved face, one +1, next tip GPS-counted, split honest), the few-metres nudge (seed point moved exactly 25.0 m toward the real spot), original spots + a load-end tap (teaches nothing, stands), re-peg count continuity + relaunch survival of the taught spot, a home tap (counts, teaches nothing), the teach-mode seed (+ rough-fix refusal), and a both-pegs day (centre drifted one bounded step; one load reads once).
